answer.generated: According to Amdahl's Law, the maximum performance benefit from parallelism is constrained by the proportion of the task that remains serial. If 20% of the task is serial, then the maximum performance improvement achievable through parallelization is limited to 80%, as the law indicates that the fraction of the task that can be parallelized is 1 minus the fraction that must remain serial. Thus, the maximum performance benefit from parallelism in this scenario is 80%, reflecting the fundamental limit set by the serial portion of the task.
